answer: Each identity registers one harbor mooring thread spool at a knoll ropewalk, posting an 80-credit bond. It files one breaking-load test: diameter, serial, knoll timestamp, and load. Auditors recompute it from the harbor log: thread load must match the diameter table, and one serial anchors one identity. A duplicate serial or off-table load burns the bond. First fee 34, kth 34+7(k-1), 1000th 7027, so 1000 fakes pay 3530500 plus 80000 locked. An honest agent pays one fee and one bond, refunded after a clean epoch. A rented-spool ring fails because a borrowed spool carries its owner's serial.
